So to maximize distinct tasks, A should choose a task that B is unlikely to also choose. Both want distinct tasks.

Given symmetry, any pair of distinct tasks yields same distinct count (4). Then total cost = sum of costs for each agent on their chosen tasks.

We need to consider that C and D will choose remaining tasks minimizing combined cost. So total cost depends on which tasks are left for C and D.

Thus A and B should choose tasks such that the remaining two tasks have minimal combined cost for C and D.
